steps.text: Gather all ingredients and preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Mix blueberries, orange juice, and 3 tablespoons sugar in an 8-inch square baking dish.
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt in a small bowl.
Cream butter and 1/2 cup sugar in a large bowl until light and fluffy. Beat in egg and vanilla. Gradually add flour mixture, stirring just until ingredients are combined.
Drop spoonfuls of batter over the blueberry mixture, covering as much filling as possible.
Bake in the preheated oven until topping is golden brown and filling bubbles, 35 to 40 minutes.

Serve and enjoy! Sweeten up your summertime with this blueberry cobbler recipe, in which a fruity filling is perfectly complemented by an irresistible cake-like topping. Perfect as is, or served alongside whipped cream or a scoop of vanilla ice cream. Home cooks love to customize the recipe with different types of berries and spices.

raw_recipe.headline: Best Ever Blueberry Cobbler
raw_recipe.description: This blueberry cobbler with fresh blueberries and orange juice is topped with a fluffy homemade batter that bakes up deliciously golden and crisp.

review.reviewBody: I've made this recipe a few times now and must say that the addition of cinnamon both into the berry mixture and cobbler batter really makes this recipe pop. I add about a 1/2 teaspoon to each, but also increase the amount of berries to 5 cups and orange juice to about 1/2 cup. Also I read many reviews of this recipe being too sweet, but I find that with fruit recipes you really have to taste the fruit before you use it to know how much sugar is needed. I rather like the cakey cobbler this recipe produces as opposed to some with a denser topping. The best compliment this recipe can get from me is that even my very picky hubby requests it regularly. Thanks for a nice basic recipe.

Terrific recipe vaulted into the five-star category by two changes. I have added 1/2 tsp of lemon zest(grated peel) and a bare sprinkle of cinnamon to the blueberry mixture on the bottom. Have added a streusel topping (over the existing two layers in the original recipe) consisting of 1/3 c. Bisquick, 1/3 c. packed brown sugar, 2 T. butter and 1/2 cup chopped pecans. The crunch and nuttiness were missing previously. Mix all streusel topping ingredients together with a pastry blender or forks and sprinkle evenly over the middle layer, baking for 35-40 minutes as usual. Vanilla ice cream is a must for most fans. Oo-o-o, LOOK OUT! It's TOO GOOD!

This is really good! But I did make some changes, namely: 

1) I used frozen blueberries. 
2) To the berry mix, I added about 2 dashes of ground nutmeg, 1/2 tsp. ground cinnamon, and 1.5 tbsp. cornstarch. I also increased the white sugar by 1 tbsp (total of 4 tbsp). The sweetness was just right.
3) I used a rectangular pan, 9.5" x 7". 

I think that the serving size is more like 4 than 6.

I reduced the butter and sugar from ½ cup to ⅓ cup, and the texture and taste of the topping was still excellent. I added a little cardamom to both the dough and the blueberries, just because I like it. I forgot to add the sugar to the blueberries and was concerned but the sweetness was still perfect. I suppose that it varies depending upon the berries. I also added a tsp. of cornstarch to the berries because someone commented that the fruit was runny. I topped the dough with some sanding sugar. The cobbler was well received and I couldn't have been happier with it.

Made it vegan and gluten free with flax egg, vegan butter, and Bob's Red Mill 1:1 gluten free flour. It was delicious, perfect. "Vegan" recipes are too much, it's better just to take normal recipes and substitute ingredients.

As suggested in comments, I increased the blueberries a half cup (3.5 cups) and fresh OJ to 1/3 cup. We loved the flavors and juicy berry syrup this created. I prepared the delicious cobbler in 2 smaller square Pyrex dishes. The bottom one needed an additional ten minutes in the oven. I’m making another cobbler this afternoon. Love how our house smells while baking!
Berry very good! I substituted a little lemon juice for the orange juice

I used 4 cup blueberries, upped the orange juice and sugar in the blueberry portion. Then added 1 Tablespoon cornstarch. This is a great recipe the orange juice makes for a unique taste. My husband loves it and it doesn’t have so much breading on top.

Excellent recipe - I made it for company that didn't show up so ate the whole thing myself! Following other readers' suggestions, I made it almost exactly as described but with the following exceptions:
+ Cinnamon (1/2 tsp)
+ 2 Tbsp corn starch in the fruit
+ 1 extra cup of fruit (for a total of 4 cups)

Absolutely to die for, this will go into my "keepers" recipes.

Super easy recipe! Doubled it for a 9x13” pan and sprinkled brown sugar over top before baking. Delicious!!
I made it for my husband's men group. It was a big hit! I think the OJ made the berries stand out. I made it as stated and was excited when my husband said,"It looks just like the picture!"

This is the BEST cobbler I can remember eating. My changes were to make batter with all ingredients but blueberries, then fold blueberries into batter before baking. I did add a smidge of nutmeg (Mom's voice in my head) and 1/2 tsp cinnamon.

Easy and delicious! I've made it twice now and use frozen blueberries and last time I added a pinch of tapioca starch to firm up the blueberry mixture but forgot to do it this time and it was better last time.
So delicious and easy to make. Based on some other reviews, I added a 1/4 tsp of nutmeg and 1/2 tsp of cinnamon to the berry mixture. I will be making this again!
I did add a little cinnamon. Best cobbler ever!

It’s great even straight from the fridge without the ice cream! Like the description says it’s not too sweet and just perfect. I only added a pinch of clear gel (like fine cornstarch) to firm up the berry mixture.

The addition of cinnamon was a fantastic addition. i followed the recipe exactly. Smelled yummy cooking, and people could hardly wait to dive in. No left overs should I say. Very good recipe and will be making again. It is a great basic cobbler recipe, you can use whatever fruit you wish. Love it, and recommend it.
Excellent taste. I didn't have enough blueberries so I used a cup of strawberries to make the 3 cups.

I thought this was really, really good. The topping is more like a cakey sugar cookie but I thought it was delicious. The only change I made to the recipe was sprinkling a little cornstarch on my berries because they were frozen, and used a mixture of blueberry and raspberry. Super fast and easy. Fit perfectly in an 8x8 pan. EDIT: 4 years later and still using this recipe! I throw in a little cinnamon now and a tiny bit of almond extract, and have used all types of berry combos. It's a keeper.
